scenarios.requirement: A build step runs, with its command line first in the output, while another thread holds a lock at the moment of the fork: the child calls nothing that takes a lock (the staging is proved live first)
A folder the child cannot enter is named on its terminal, as a shell names it, while another thread holds a lock at the moment of the fork

A terminal the system refuses a child (it belongs to another session) is named on that terminal, and the child ends as a command that cannot run, while another thread holds a lock at the moment of the fork

The words of a start that failed are the same in each stream: the build's command line then its failed line, a program or folder named on a terminal (127), a terminal named by path on the editor's own stderr, a child's own error pipe, and nothing for a child whose errors go nowhere

A child that cannot run tells the editor the stage and errno on a report pipe, which the editor traces when the end is delivered; one that runs is traced as having run; no descriptor is left open either way
An editor whose 0, 1 and 2 are closed still gets the report of a start that cannot run: the editor traces the stage and errno, and the record never reaches the program's file
F9 on a C file puts the compiler's command line in Messages, ahead of the compiler's own diagnostic and the build's summary, in the terminal editor
F9 on a C file starts the compiler, links the program and traces that the build ran in the X11 editor, which runs a font thread
F9 on a C file starts the compiler, links the program and traces that the build ran in the Wayland editor, which runs a font thread
A compiler that does not exist is named in the error row, the terminal editor goes on taking keys, and the owner traces that the exec failed with error 2
With no compiler to be found the X11 editor, which runs a font thread, traces that the exec failed with error 2 and goes on taking keys
With no compiler to be found the Wayland editor, which runs a font thread, traces that the exec failed with error 2 and goes on taking keys
The terminal editor is one thread and has no Pango font thread
The X11 editor has more than one thread, one of them the Pango font thread
The Wayland editor has more than one thread, one of them the Pango font thread
A signal a child receives before its exec never runs a handler of the editor's: one ignored by default reaches no handler, and a fault ends the child by the signal
